title: City payees that lobby Washington or fund national political groups
question: Which organisations the City pays also pay federal lobbyists or give to national political groups, and do their tax returns say so?
finding: 4 City payees are named as federal lobbying clients, with $3.9 million reported by their lobbyists since 2013; every charity among them also reports lobbying on its own tax returns. City payees gave $883,106 to national political groups registered under section 527, $732,048 of it from Pacific Gas & Electric Co and Orrick Herrington & Sutcliffe.
how: Federal lobbying: every client in the Senate's lobbying filings whose name equals a City-paid organisation after tidying, one report per client, firm and quarter (an amendment replaces the original), income or expenses as reported. Tax returns: the yes/no lobbying question and the lobbying-fees line on each Form 990 on file. Political groups: Schedule A of IRS Form 8872 where the contributor's name equals a payee the City paid $1 million or more; repeated lines from amended reports counted once.
limits: City money is not shown to have paid for either. The lobbying data reaches only clients whose name matched exactly, so the list is short and incomplete. A nonprofit can truthfully answer no if the lobbying was done by a separate affiliate with a similar name, or if its return covers a different legal entity. Payments to ActBlue Technical Services ($2.7 million from City-paid nonprofits) are left out: it is a donation-processing platform, and those lines look like processing charges rather than political gifts.
